findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be instantiated — abstract methods left unimplemented
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from DetectorHandler (with a concrete `evaluate` stub) to `StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]` with just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`), none of which are implemented here. MetricAlertDetectorHandler is registered as `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler`, and `Detector.detector_handler` in src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py instantiates it via `group_type.detector_handler(self)` — that call will now raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Neither `detector_handler` nor `process_detectors` guards against instantiation errors, so a single Detector of this type would raise an uncaught exception and abort processing of the entire detector batch. Previously the class was instantiable and safely returned no results. Either keep the old evaluate() stub until the stateful implementation exists, or implement the abstract methods.

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring for `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` states: 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`.' The signature and implementation were changed in this PR to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, so the docstring now contradicts the actual contract and will mislead implementers of the abstract method. It should say the results are returned as a dict keyed by group key.

findings.title: Occurrence builder mock ignores the `value` argument, so tests assert occurrences built with wrong values
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value` but never uses it, and several tests pass a value that does not match the data packet actually evaluated. For example, in `test_state_results_multi_group` the packet has `{'group_1': 6, 'group_2': 10}` but the expected occurrence for 'group_2' is built with value 6 (line 191); in `test_results_on_change`/`test_dedupe` the evaluated value is 100/8 but the expected occurrence is built with 6. Because the mock discards `value`, the tests pass regardless, so a regression where `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the wrong value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (the new hook this PR adds) would not be caught. The mock should incorporate `value` into the built occurrence/event data (or the test expectations should use the real values).
